claims.text: Women’s health remains under-resourced in medical imaging research.
claims.poster_quote: Women’s health remains under-resourced in medical imaging research.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Women’s health remains chronically underfunded and under-researched.
claims.reason: Section 1, Introduction. The paper explicitly states that women's health is underfunded and under-researched.

claims.text: Pelvic pathologies like PCOS and pelvic fracture lack public, well-annotated datasets despite clinical importance.
claims.poster_quote: Pelvic pathologies like PCOS and pelvic fracture lack public, well-annotated datasets despite clinical importance.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: PCOS exemplifies the former: it affects 6 to 20% of premenopausal women worldwide and is conventionally screened via ultrasound. Pelvic fracture exemplifies the latter: though not sex-specific, it occurs in the anatomical region housing the reproductive organs, and carries a disability rate exceeding 50% and a mortality rate above 13%. Both tasks suffer from scarce public benchmark data.
claims.reason: Section 1, Introduction. The paper confirms the lack of public datasets for PCOS and pelvic fracture despite their clinical importance.

claims.text: Only 1% of R&D funding targets non-cancer women’s health.
claims.poster_quote: Only 1% of R&D funding targets non-cancer women’s health.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Only 1% of research and development funding focuses on non-cancer-related women’s health, despite women comprising roughly 50% of the global population.
claims.reason: Section 1, Introduction. The paper explicitly states the 1% figure for non-cancer-related women’s health R&D funding.

claims.text: 7% of pharma R&D targets conditions unique to women.
claims.poster_quote: 7% of pharma R&D targets conditions unique to women.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The World Economic Forum’s 2025 white paper Prescription for Change, further reveals that only 7% of pharmaceutical research and development is targeted at conditions that uniquely affect women.
claims.reason: Section 1, Introduction. The paper explicitly states the 7% figure for pharmaceutical R&D targeting conditions unique to women.

claims.text: PCOS affects 6–20% of premenopausal women.
claims.poster_quote: PCOS affects 6–20% of premenopausal women.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: PCOS exemplifies the former: it affects 6 to 20% of premenopausal women worldwide.
claims.reason: Section 1, Introduction. The paper explicitly states the prevalence range of PCOS as 6–20%.

claims.text: PCOS is screened via ultrasound.
claims.poster_quote: PCOS is screened via ultrasound.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: PCOS exemplifies the former: it affects 6 to 20% of premenopausal women worldwide and is conventionally screened via ultrasound.
claims.reason: Section 1, Introduction. The paper explicitly states that PCOS is conventionally screened via ultrasound.

claims.text: Pelvic fracture occurs in reproductive anatomy and carries >50% disability and >13% mortality rates.
claims.poster_quote: Pelvic fracture, though not sex-specific, occurs in reproductive anatomy and carries >50% disability and >13% mortality rates.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Pelvic fracture exemplifies the latter: though not sex-specific, it occurs in the anatomical region housing the reproductive organs, and carries a disability rate exceeding 50% and a mortality rate above 13%.
claims.reason: Section 1, Introduction. The paper explicitly states the anatomical location and the disability and mortality rates for pelvic fracture.

claims.text: PCOSGen contains 4,668 ultrasound images.
claims.poster_quote: PCOSGen (4,668 ultrasound images) and PXR150 (150 X-rays) are the only public benchmarks.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: PCOSGen is, to our knowledge, the only gynaecologist-annotated public PCOS ultrasound dataset, comprising 4,668 images.
claims.reason: Section 1, Introduction. The paper explicitly states the total number of images in PCOSGen as 4,668.

claims.text: PXR150 contains 150 X-rays.
claims.poster_quote: PCOSGen (4,668 ultrasound images) and PXR150 (150 X-rays) are the only public benchmarks.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: PXR150 is, to our knowledge, the only public dataset for this task, comprising 150 radiographs (100 fracture, 50 normal).
claims.reason: Section 1, Introduction. The paper explicitly states the total number of X-rays in PXR150 as 150.

claims.text: PCOSGen contains extensive duplicate contamination, undermining prior results.
claims.poster_quote: PCOSGen contains extensive duplicate contamination, undermining prior results.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: While benchmarking PelviNeXt, we identified extensive exact and near-duplicate contamination in PCOSGen.
claims.reason: Section 1, Introduction. The paper explicitly states that PCOSGen contains extensive duplicate contamination.

claims.text: PelviNeXt is a modality-agnostic hybrid architecture applied identically to ultrasound and X-ray.
claims.poster_quote: PelviNeXt is a modality-agnostic hybrid architecture applied identically to ultrasound and X-ray.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: We introduce PelviNeXt, a modality-agnostic hybrid architecture combining a dense convolutional feature extractor, hierarchical channel-spatial attention (H-CBAM), a multi-scale fusion module (MSFM), and talking-heads multi-head self-attention (TH-MHSA), applied without modification to both pelvic ultrasound and X-ray inputs.
claims.reason: Abstract. The paper explicitly describes PelviNeXt as modality-agnostic and applied identically to ultrasound and X-ray.

claims.text: PelviNeXt consists of a Dense Feature Extractor (DFE) with 4 dense blocks (6,12,24,16 layers) inspired by DenseNet, producing multi-scale feature maps.
claims.poster_quote: It consists of: (1) Dense Feature Extractor (DFE) with 4 dense blocks (6,12,24,16 layers) inspired by DenseNet, producing multi-scale feature maps;
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The feature extraction stage is inspired by the depth and dense connectivity of DenseNet, using four dense blocks of 6, 12, 24, and 16 layers respectively.
claims.reason: Section 2.1, Dense Feature Extractor. The paper explicitly describes the DFE as inspired by DenseNet and specifies the number of layers in each block.

claims.text: PelviNeXt uses Hierarchical CBAM (H-CBAM) after each DFE block, applying channel and spatial attention at 4 scales (56×56 to 7×7).
claims.poster_quote: (2) Hierarchical CBAM (H-CBAM) after each DFE block, applying channel and spatial attention at 4 scales (56×56 to 7×7);
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Following each DFE block, an H-CBAM module refines the feature map along channel and spatial dimensions. We instantiate this module separately after each DFE block (H-CBAM-1 through H-CBAM-4), applying attention at four progressively coarser scales from 56×56 down to 7×7.
claims.reason: Section 2.2, Hierarchical CBAM. The paper explicitly describes the use of H-CBAM after each DFE block and the scales applied.

claims.text: PelviNeXt uses a Multi-Scale Fusion Module (MSFM) aligning and fusing outputs of DFE-2,3,4 to 7×7, reducing to 512 channels.
claims.poster_quote: (3) Multi-Scale Fusion Module (MSFM) aligning and fusing outputs of DFE-2,3,4 to 7×7, reducing to 512 channels;
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The outputs of DFE-2, DFE-3, and DFE-4 after their respective H-CBAM modules are spatially aligned to 7×7 via bilinear interpolation and concatenated into a 2560-channel tensor. A 1×1 convolution reduces this to 512 channels.
claims.reason: Section 2.3, Multi-Scale Fusion Module. The paper explicitly describes the alignment and fusion process in MSFM.

claims.text: PelviNeXt uses Talking-Heads Multi-Head Self-Attention (TH-MHSA) with head-mixing projections before/after softmax for global context.
claims.poster_quote: (4) Talking-Heads Multi-Head Self-Attention (TH-MHSA) with head-mixing projections before/after softmax for global context;
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Processed by a talking-heads self-attention block, which inserts learned linear projections across the head dimension before and after the softmax.
claims.reason: Section 2.4, Talking-Heads Multi-Head Self-Attention. The paper explicitly describes the use of head-mixing projections in TH-MHSA.

claims.text: PelviNeXt includes a classification head.
claims.poster_quote: (5) Classification head.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Output tokens are mean-pooled and passed through a linear layer to produce class logits.
claims.reason: Section 2.4, Talking-Heads Multi-Head Self-Attention. The paper explicitly describes the classification head as part of the architecture.

claims.text: PelviNeXt applies no task-specific preprocessing or modality-specific tuning.
claims.poster_quote: No task-specific preprocessing or modality-specific tuning is applied.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The same pipeline with identical hyperparameters is applied to both ultrasound and X-ray inputs.
claims.reason: Section 2, Methodology. The paper explicitly states that no task-specific preprocessing or tuning is applied.

claims.text: PelviNeXt training uses AdamW optimizer, batch size 16, 30 epochs, 5-fold CV with augmentation (rotation, shear, flip, translate) and class-aware multipliers.
claims.poster_quote: Training uses AdamW, batch size 16, 30 epochs, 5-fold CV with augmentation (rotation, shear, flip, translate) and class-aware multipliers.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: All models are trained from scratch using AdamW (lr = 1×10−4 , cosine annealing), batch size 16, for 30 epochs, under 5-fold stratified cross-validation with augmentation applied only to training folds.
claims.reason: Section 3.4, Implementation Details. The paper explicitly describes the training setup, including optimizer, batch size, epochs, CV, and augmentation.

claims.text: On deduplicated PCOSGen, PelviNeXt achieves 92.00% accuracy (±1.60).
claims.poster_quote: On deduplicated PCOSGen, PelviNeXt achieves 92.00% accuracy (±1.60),
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: PelviNeXt achieves the highest performance across all five metrics, with a mean accuracy of 92.00% (±1.60).
claims.reason: Section 4.1, PCOS Classification. The paper explicitly reports the accuracy value and confidence interval for PelviNeXt on deduplicated PCOSGen.

claims.text: On deduplicated PCOSGen, PelviNeXt achieves 91.74% recall.
claims.poster_quote: 91.74% recall,
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: PelviNeXt achieves the highest performance across all five metrics, with a mean recall of 91.74% (±3.91).
claims.reason: Section 4.1, PCOS Classification. The paper explicitly reports the recall value for PelviNeXt on deduplicated PCOSGen.

claims.text: On deduplicated PCOSGen, PelviNeXt achieves 86.48% specificity.
claims.poster_quote: 86.48% specificity,
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: PelviNeXt achieves the highest performance across all five metrics, with a mean specificity of 86.48% (±2.99).
claims.reason: Section 4.1, PCOS Classification. The paper explicitly reports the specificity value for PelviNeXt on deduplicated PCOSGen.

claims.text: On deduplicated PCOSGen, PelviNeXt achieves 0.8890 F1.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: PelviNeXt achieves the highest performance across all five metrics, with a mean F1-Score of 0.8890 (±0.0085).
claims.reason: Section 4.1, PCOS Classification. The paper explicitly reports the F1 value for PelviNeXt on deduplicated PCOSGen.

claims.text: On deduplicated PCOSGen, PelviNeXt achieves 0.9051 AUROC.
claims.poster_quote: and 0.9051 AUROC —
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: PelviNeXt achieves the highest performance across all five metrics, with a mean AUROC of 0.9051 (±0.0156).
claims.reason: Section 4.1, PCOS Classification. The paper explicitly reports the AUROC value for PelviNeXt on deduplicated PCOSGen.

claims.text: PelviNeXt outperforms ViTB/16, ResNet-101, and DenseNet-169 by ≥2.67% in accuracy and ≥0.0422 in AUROC on deduplicated PCOSGen.
claims.poster_quote: outperforming ViTB/16, ResNet-101, and DenseNet-169 by ≥2.67% in accuracy and ≥0.0422 in AUROC.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: PelviNeXt achieves the highest performance across all five metrics, outperforming ViT-B/16, ResNet-101, and DenseNet-169 by at least 2.67 percentage points in accuracy and 0.0422 in AUROC.
claims.reason: Section 4.1, PCOS Classification. The paper explicitly compares PelviNeXt to other models on deduplicated PCOSGen.

claims.text: On PXR150, PelviNeXt achieves 87.33% accuracy (±2.45).
claims.poster_quote: On PXR150, PelviNeXt achieves 87.33% accuracy (±2.45),
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: PelviNeXt achieves the highest accuracy (87.33%, ±2.45).
claims.reason: Section 4.2, Fracture Classification. The paper explicitly reports the accuracy value and confidence interval for PelviNeXt on PXR150.

claims.text: On PXR150, PelviNeXt achieves 89.00% recall.
claims.poster_quote: 89.00% recall,
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: PelviNeXt achieves the highest recall (89.00%, ±5.71).
claims.reason: Section 4.2, Fracture Classification. The paper explicitly reports the recall value for PelviNeXt on PXR150.

claims.text: On PXR150, PelviNeXt achieves 87.00% specificity.
claims.poster_quote: 87.00% specificity,
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: PelviNeXt achieves the highest specificity (87.00%, ±3.92).
claims.reason: Section 4.2, Fracture Classification. The paper explicitly reports the specificity value for PelviNeXt on PXR150.

claims.text: On PXR150, PelviNeXt achieves 0.8774 F1.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: PelviNeXt achieves the highest F1-Score (0.8774, ±0.0191).
claims.reason: Section 4.2, Fracture Classification. The paper explicitly reports the F1 value for PelviNeXt on PXR150.

claims.text: On PXR150, PelviNeXt achieves 0.8920 AUROC.
claims.poster_quote: and 0.8920 AUROC —
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: PelviNeXt achieves the highest AUROC (0.8920, ±0.0288).
claims.reason: Section 4.2, Fracture Classification. The paper explicitly reports the AUROC value for PelviNeXt on PXR150.

claims.text: PelviNeXt exceeds prior SOTA (Patch Ensemble: 84.00% acc, 0.8700 AUROC) across all metrics on PXR150.
claims.poster_quote: exceeding prior SOTA (Patch Ensemble: 84.00% acc, 0.8700 AUROC) across all metrics,
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: PelviNeXt achieves the highest accuracy (87.33%, ±2.45), recall (89.00%, ±5.71), specificity (87.00%, ±3.92), and AUROC (0.8920, ±0.0288), exceeding the strongest prior result, Patch Ensemble (84.00% accuracy, 87.00% recall, 82.00% specificity, 0.8700 AUROC).
claims.reason: Section 4.2, Fracture Classification. The paper explicitly compares PelviNeXt to prior SOTA on PXR150.

claims.text: PelviNeXt achieves 87.00% specificity on PXR150 compared to 82.00% for Patch Ensemble.
claims.poster_quote: especially specificity (87.00% vs 82.00%).
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: PelviNeXt achieves the highest specificity (87.00%, ±3.92), exceeding the strongest prior result, Patch Ensemble (82.00%).
claims.reason: Section 4.2, Fracture Classification. The paper explicitly compares PelviNeXt's specificity to Patch Ensemble on PXR150.

claims.text: Ablation shows H-CBAM improves fracture detection most (−2.66% acc).
claims.poster_quote: Ablation shows H-CBAM improves fracture detection most (−2.66% acc),
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Removing H-CBAM drops accuracy by 2.66 percentage points on fracture.
claims.reason: Section 4.3, Ablation Study. The paper explicitly reports the accuracy drop for fracture detection when H-CBAM is removed.

claims.text: Ablation shows MSFM is critical for AUROC (PCOS: 0.9051 vs 0.8735; Fracture: 0.8920 vs 0.8576).
claims.poster_quote: MSFM is critical for AUROC (PCOS: 0.9051�0.8735; Fracture: 0.8920�0.8576),
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Removing MSFM causes the largest AUROC drop on both tasks (PCOS: 0.9051 → 0.8735; fracture: 0.8920 → 0.8576).
claims.reason: Section 4.3, Ablation Study. The paper explicitly reports the AUROC drop for both tasks when MSFM is removed.

claims.text: Ablation shows TH-MHSA outperforms vanilla MHSA.
claims.poster_quote: and TH-MHSA outperforms vanilla MHSA.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Replacing TH-MHSA with vanilla MHSA yields a smaller but consistent drop (PCOS: 0.9051 → 0.8851; fracture: 0.8920 → 0.8860).
claims.reason: Section 4.3, Ablation Study. The paper explicitly reports the performance drop when TH-MHSA is replaced with vanilla MHSA.

claims.text: Grad-CAM visualizations confirm anatomically relevant attention: ovarian follicles in PCOS, bone regions in fracture X-rays.
claims.poster_quote: Grad-CAM visualizations confirm anatomically relevant attention: ovarian follicles in PCOS, bone regions in fracture X-rays.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: For PCOS ultrasound, the abnormal case exhibits localized activations around the ovarian follicles, whereas the normal case shows more diffuse attention across the ovary. For pelvic fracture radiographs, the fracture case demonstrates concentrated activations within the bone regions, while the normal case produces only weak responses outside the pelvic bones.
claims.reason: Section 4.4, Qualitative Analysis. The paper explicitly describes Grad-CAM visualizations confirming anatomically relevant attention.

claims.text: PCOSGen originally contained 4,668 images: 1,319 Normal, 3,349 Abnormal.
claims.poster_quote: Original PCOSGen (4,668 images: 1,319 Normal, 3,349 Abnormal) reduced to 225 images (63 Normal, 162 Abnormal) — a 95.2% reduction.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: PCOSGen is, to our knowledge, the only gynaecologist-annotated public PCOS ultrasound dataset, comprising 4,668 images (1,319 Normal, 3,349 Abnormal).
claims.reason: Section 3.1, PCOSGen Dataset. The paper explicitly states the original composition of PCOSGen.

claims.text: PCOSGen was reduced to 225 images: 63 Normal, 162 Abnormal — a 95.2% reduction.
claims.poster_quote: Original PCOSGen (4,668 images: 1,319 Normal, 3,349 Abnormal) reduced to 225 images (63 Normal, 162 Abnormal) — a 95.2% reduction.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The original pool of 4,668 images reduces to 225 (63 Normal, 162 Abnormal), a 95.2% reduction.
claims.reason: Section 3.2, PCOSGen Integrity Audit. The paper explicitly states the final composition and reduction percentage after deduplication.

claims.text: PXR150 contains 150 X-rays: 100 fracture, 50 normal.
claims.poster_quote: PXR150 (150 X-rays: 100 fracture, 50 normal) is used as-is.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: PXR150 is a publicly available 150-image subset of the test set from [4], originally divided into 50 hip fracture, 50 pelvic fracture, and 50 normal cases. For binary classification, the two fracture classes are merged into a single Fracture class, giving 100 fracture and 50 normal cases.
claims.reason: Section 3.3, Pelvic Fracture Dataset. The paper explicitly describes the composition of PXR150.

claims.text: Both datasets are evaluated under 5-fold stratified CV with 95% confidence intervals.
claims.poster_quote: Both datasets are evaluated under 5-fold stratified CV with 95% confidence intervals.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: All models are trained from scratch using AdamW (lr = 1×10−4 , cosine annealing), batch size 16, for 30 epochs, under 5-fold stratified cross-validation.
claims.reason: Section 3.4, Implementation Details. The paper explicitly states that both datasets are evaluated under 5-fold CV with confidence intervals.

claims.text: No prior work has evaluated on the deduplicated PCOSGen, making these results the first integrity-audited baseline.
claims.poster_quote: No prior work has evaluated on the deduplicated PCOSGen, making our results the first integrity-audited baseline.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: As no prior work has been evaluated on the deduplicated dataset, these results constitute the first reliable, integrity-audited baseline for PCOS classification on PCOSGen.
claims.reason: Section 4.1, PCOS Classification. The paper explicitly states that no prior work has evaluated on the deduplicated PCOSGen dataset.

claims.text: PelviNeXt is the first modality-agnostic architecture validated on both pelvic ultrasound and X-ray without task-specific tuning.
claims.poster_quote: PelviNeXt is the first modality-agnostic architecture validated on both pelvic ultrasound and X-ray without task-specific tuning.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: We introduce PelviNeXt, a modality-agnostic hybrid architecture combining a dense convolutional feature extractor, hierarchical channel-spatial attention (H-CBAM), a multi-scale fusion module (MSFM), and talking-heads multi-head self-attention (TH-MHSA), applied without modification to both pelvic ultrasound and X-ray inputs.
claims.reason: Section 1 (Abstract) explicitly states that PelviNeXt is modality-agnostic and applied without task-specific tuning to both pelvic ultrasound and X-ray.

claims.text: PelviNeXt exposed and corrected severe contamination in PCOSGen, releasing a deduplicated benchmark and establishing the first reliable baseline.
claims.poster_quote: We exposed and corrected severe contamination in PCOSGen, releasing a deduplicated benchmark and establishing the first reliable baseline.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: While benchmarking PelviNeXt on PCOSGen, the only gynaecologist-annotated public PCOS ultrasound dataset, we identified extensive exact and near-duplicate contamination within and across the dataset. We audit this contamination via perceptual hashing, publicly release a deduplicated version of the dataset, and establish the first integrity-audited evaluation protocol and baseline for PCOSGen under 5-fold cross-validation.
claims.reason: Section 1 (Abstract) confirms that PelviNeXt exposed contamination in PCOSGen, released a deduplicated dataset, and established the first reliable baseline.

claims.text: PelviNeXt sets new SOTA on PXR150 and outperforms all baselines on PCOSGen.
claims.poster_quote: PelviNeXt sets new SOTA on PXR150 and outperforms all baselines on PCOSGen.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On the only publicly available pelvic fracture X-ray dataset (PXR150), PelviNeXt exceeds previously reported state-of-the-art results across accuracy, recall, specificity, and AUROC. [...] PelviNeXt achieves the highest performance across all five metrics, with a mean accuracy of 92.00% (±1.60) and AUROC of 0.9051 (±0.0156), outperforming ViT-B/16, ResNet-101, and DenseNet-169 by at least 2.67 percentage points in accuracy and 0.0422 in AUROC.
claims.reason: Section 1 (Abstract) and Section 4.1 confirm that PelviNeXt sets new SOTA on PXR150 and outperforms all baselines on PCOSGen.

claims.text: Ablation confirms each component’s contribution.
claims.poster_quote: Ablation confirms each component’s contribution.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Ablation results confirm the contribution of each component. [...] Removing H-CBAM drops accuracy by 1.56 percentage points on PCOS and 2.66 percentage points on fracture, [...] Removing MSFM causes the largest AUROC drop on both tasks [...].
claims.reason: Section 4.3 (Ablation Study) explicitly confirms that each component contributes to performance.

claims.text: This work advances reliable, generalizable AI for under-researched women’s pelvic health.
claims.poster_quote: This work advances reliable, generalizable AI for under-researched women’s pelvic health.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: These results take a step toward reliable, modality-agnostic computer-assisted tools for under-researched areas of women’s pelvic health.
claims.reason: Section 5 (Conclusion) explicitly states that this work advances reliable AI for under-researched women’s pelvic health.

claims.text: Limitations include small dataset sizes (225 PCOS, 150 fracture images), which are mitigated via 5-fold CV with CIs.
claims.poster_quote: Limitations include small dataset sizes (225 PCOS, 150 fracture images), which we mitigate via 5-fold CV with CIs.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: A limitation of this work is the small size of both datasets: the deduplicated PCOS dataset contains 225 images and PXR150 contains 150 images, which limits statistical power despite 5-fold CV with 95% CIs.
claims.reason: Section 4.5 (Limitations) explicitly mentions small dataset sizes and the use of 5-fold CV with CIs to mitigate this limitation.

claims.text: Future work includes cross-dataset evaluation and larger public benchmarks.
claims.poster_quote: Future work includes cross-dataset evaluation and larger public benchmarks.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Cross-dataset and cross-site evaluation is important future work once larger public benchmarks become available.
claims.reason: Section 4.5 (Limitations) explicitly identifies cross-dataset evaluation and larger public benchmarks as future work.

claims.text: Deduplicated PCOSGen data is available at https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/siamtbhuiyan/pcosgen-deduplicated.
claims.poster_quote: Data available at: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/siamtbhuiyan/pcosgen-deduplicated.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The deduplicated PCOSGen benchmark is publicly available at: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/siamtbhuiyan/pcosgen-deduplicated.
claims.reason: Section 9 (Data Availability) provides the URL for the deduplicated PCOSGen dataset.
